I build and audit evaluations for tool-using agents. The question I keep returning to is whether an
eval's number means what it is taken to mean.

An eval makes three claims — about the harness, the benchmark, and the metric — and each can fail
quietly while the run reports success. Three studies, in that order.

{{< include figures/three-claims.qmd >}}

::: {.figcap}
Each claim has its own failure mode, and each fails while the run still reports success.
:::

::: {.spaced}

### Can the environment control what the model knows?

[What's the right way to filter tool outputs in Inspect?](posts/filtering-tool-outputs-in-inspect.qmd)
· Aug 2026\
[The interception point that looks correct fails open silently: the eval passes with the control
skipped, and nothing in the log says so.]{.finding}

### Does the task still elicit the behaviour?

[69% → 11% → 0%: three generations on Apollo's insider-trading eval](posts/insider-trading-eval-saturated.qmd)
· Sep 2026\
[The 2023 result replicates, then bounds under 1% on a current model — but 298 of 300 runs leave the
authored scenario on turn one, so the zero measures departure from the script.]{.finding}

### Does the scorer detect the behaviour?

[When do AI agents leak restricted information?](posts/when-agents-leak-restricted-information.qmd)
· Sep 2026\
[Naming the restricted field changed nothing; naming the tool-call channel took disclosure to zero.
Then information derived from the restricted value kept flowing, while the metric read zero.]{.finding}

:::
